factual_claims.claim: Nordecon’s financial performance weakened in 2025 compared with the previous year, although the group strengthened its order book and expects business volumes to increase in 2026.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Key figures section states revenue decreased by 7%, gross margin fell to 6.5% from 7.5%, operating profit declined to €5.7m from €8.1m, net profit fell to €2.5m from €5.2m. Order book increased by 30% to €273.1m. Management expects business volumes to increase in 2026 based on order book size and market outlook.

factual_claims.claim: Revenue declined by 7% to €208.3 million, primarily because Buildings segment revenue fell by approximately 10% to €168.3 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Key figures table shows revenue decreased from €223,925k (2024) to €208,281k (2025) - a 7% decline. Segment reporting section states Buildings revenue was €168,302k (2025) vs €187,573k (2024), a ~10% decrease.

factual_claims.claim: Infrastructure revenue increased by 10% to €39.9 million, supported by road construction, maintenance and Rail Baltica-related work.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Segment reporting section states Infrastructure revenue increased from €36,299k (2024) to €39,902k (2025) - a 10% increase. Financial review mentions revenue came from road construction, maintenance, and Rail Baltica projects.

factual_claims.claim: Buildings still represented the majority of revenue, with an 81% share, while Infrastructure accounted for 19%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Segment revenue table shows Buildings contributed 81% of total revenue and Infrastructure 19% in 2025.

factual_claims.claim: Profitability deteriorated as gross profit decreased to €13.5 million from €16.8 million and gross margin fell to 6.5% from 7.5%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Financial review states gross profit was €13,535k (2025) vs €16,770k (2024). Gross margin decreased to 6.5% from 7.5%.

factual_claims.claim: Operating profit declined by 30% to €5.7 million, reducing the operating margin to 2.7% from 3.6%, below the group’s target of consistently exceeding 3%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Financial review states operating profit was €5,651k (2025) vs €8,061k (2024) - a ~30% decrease. Operating margin fell to 2.7% from 3.6%. Directors' report states operating margin target is consistently above 3%.

factual_claims.claim: EBITDA fell to €8.3 million from €11.0 million, and the EBITDA margin declined to 4.0% from 4.9%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Key figures table shows EBITDA was €8,250k (2025) vs €11,025k (2024). EBITDA margin decreased to 4.0% from 4.9%.

factual_claims.claim: Lower administrative expenses, which decreased by 14% to €6.8 million due mainly to reduced performance-based pay, partly offset the pressure on operating results.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 11 shows administrative expenses decreased from €7,878k (2024) to €6,814k (2025) - a 14% decrease. The decrease is attributed to lower staff costs including reduced performance-based pay.

factual_claims.claim: Net profit declined by 51% to €2.5 million, while profit attributable to Nordecon’s owners fell to €1.4 million from €3.8 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Consolidated statement of comprehensive income shows net profit was €2,545k (2025) vs €5,165k (2024) - a 51% decrease. Profit attributable to owners was €1,439k vs €3,827k.

factual_claims.claim: Earnings per share decreased to €0.05 from €0.12.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 7 shows basic and diluted EPS was €0.05 in 2025 vs €0.12 in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: Results were significantly affected by higher net finance costs, which increased to €3.0 million from €2.3 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Consolidated statement of comprehensive income shows net finance costs were €2,965k (2025) vs €2,333k (2024).

factual_claims.claim: The main factor was a €750 thousand foreign-exchange loss arising from the weakening of the Ukrainian hryvnia against the euro, compared with €258 thousand in 2024.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 13 states foreign exchange loss was €750k in 2025 vs €258k in 2024, specifically from weakening of Ukrainian hryvnia.

factual_claims.claim: Credit losses also increased to €354 thousand from €20 thousand.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Note 9 states credit losses were €354k in 2025 vs €20k in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: Operating cash flow remained positive at €1.2 million, compared with €1.1 million in 2024.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Consolidated statement of cash flows shows operating activities produced €1,204k in 2025 vs €1,075k in 2024.

factual_claims.claim: However, investing activities used €2.8 million, including €2.9 million placed in long-term deposits to secure guarantee limits, while financing activities used €1.2 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Cash flow statement shows investing activities used €2,767k, including €2,898k placed in long-term deposits. Financing activities used €1,194k.

factual_claims.claim: Consequently, cash and cash equivalents declined to €5.3 million from €8.2 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Consolidated statement of financial position shows cash and cash equivalents were €5,266k (2025) vs €8,195k (2024).

factual_claims.claim: Liquidity remained relatively constrained, with the current ratio at 0.93, broadly unchanged from 0.94 at the end of 2024.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Consolidated statement of financial position shows current ratio was 0.93 (2025) vs 0.94 (2024). Risk section notes liquidity risk remains higher than usual.

factual_claims.claim: The principal positive development was the 30% increase in the order book to €273.1 million at year-end.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Order book section states order book increased by ~30% to €273,060k at 31 Dec 2025.

factual_claims.claim: New contracts secured during the year totalled €235.0 million, including major Rail Baltica, road, public-building, defence and commercial projects.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Order book section states new contracts signed were €234,994k. Major contracts listed include Rail Baltica, road projects, public buildings (defence), and commercial buildings.

factual_claims.claim: Infrastructure’s share of the order book rose to 42% from 18%, while Buildings’ share declined to 58% from 82%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Order book section states Infrastructure accounted for 42% and Buildings for 58% of order book at end of 2025, compared to 18% and 82% at end of 2024.

factual_claims.claim: About 69% of the backlog is scheduled for execution in 2026.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Order book section states approximately 69% of order book comprises work scheduled for 2026.

factual_claims.claim: Estonia’s construction market stabilised during the year, with activity improving in the second half, although competition, rising material prices and public-investment levels remain important risks.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Key figures section states construction market stabilised with slight increase in activity in second half of year. Risk section identifies competition, material price increases, and public investment levels as key market risks.
